title: Aeroflot 5003 (1977)
summary: Aeroflot Flight 5003, an Ilyushin Il-18V carrying 98 people, crashed near Mineralnye Vody on February 15, 1977 while attempting a go-around after a missed approach. Weather included low-level clouds and fog with visibility 1020-1180 meters. The crew drifted off course during approach, realized the deviation at 1.5 kilometers from the airport, and attempted to abort the landing. During the go-around climb at low altitude, the crew pulled the nose up to 11 degrees, causing a 1.64 G overload that damaged control surfaces. The aircraft entered a steep bank and struck the ground.
probable_cause: During a missed approach go-around in low visibility, the pilot in command pulled the nose up to an excessive angle of attack, causing control surface damage and loss of control.

Aircraft hit ground at 23:17:44 at altitude of 120-130 meters while in left bank, damaging railroad at impact site.

title: Tenerife airport disaster
summary: Two Boeing 747s, KLM Flight 4805 and Pan Am Flight 1736, collided on the single runway at Los Rodeos Airport, Tenerife, on 27 March 1977, killing 583 in the deadliest accident in aviation history. Both aircraft had been diverted there after a bomb at their destination, Gran Canaria, and congestion forced departing aircraft to backtaxi along the runway. In dense fog, the KLM captain began his takeoff run believing ATC had cleared him and that the Pan Am jet, still on the runway, had vacated it.
probable_cause: Spanish investigators found the primary cause was the KLM captain's decision to take off believing ATC had issued clearance and that Pan Am had cleared the runway, despite Pan Am radioing it would report when clear; Dutch investigators emphasized a mutual misunderstanding in the radio communications between the KLM crew and ATC.

title: Southern Airways 242
summary: Southern Airways Flight 242 suffered total loss of thrust from both engines while descending through a severe thunderstorm with embedded cells. The crew had been advised of severe weather but proceeded based on radar display interpretation that was misleading due to radar attenuation of the storm's peak convective activity. The aircraft encountered a massive amount of rain and hail that broke the windshield and caused both engines to ingest water and hail, resulting in compressor stalling and flameout. The crew successfully glided the aircraft unpowered to a forced landing on Georgia State Route 381.
probable_cause: Total loss of thrust from both engines caused by ingestion of massive amounts of water and hail during penetration of severe thunderstorm cell, in combination with thrust lever movement that induced severe stalling and major damage to the engine compressors. The crew's misinterpretation of weather radar attenuation contributed to the decision to penetrate the storm.

The Pratt & Whitney JT8D-7A engines ingested a massive amount of water and hail causing major damage to the compressors and flameout
The crew attempted unsuccessfully to restart the engines, gliding down unpowered, executing a forced landing on Georgia State Route 381

title: Delta Air Lines 1080
summary: Delta Air Lines Flight 1080, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar, experienced a critical control problem on 12 April 1977. During the pre-takeoff control surface check, the left elevator became stuck in a fully upward position. After rotation, the aircraft pitched up aggressively despite full forward column input. The crew exhausted all available control procedures including trim systems and hydraulic checks. Over 55 minutes, using differential thrust and moving passengers forward, the crew landed safely.
probable_cause: Water corrosion of the left elevator aft drive quadrant from pressurization cycles caused the bearing to jam. The FAA's initial inspection directive was insufficient to prevent flight with a jammed elevator.

title: 1977 Dan-Air Boeing 707 crash
summary: A Boeing 707-321C cargo aircraft detached its right horizontal stabilizer during approach to Lusaka on 14 May 1977. The crew lost pitch control and the aircraft nose-dived from 800 feet, impacting the ground and killing all six occupants. Investigation determined the stabilizer failed due to metal fatigue in the rear spar, caused by a design modification that altered how the tailplane handled gust loads. The crack had gone undetected due to its concealed internal location within the structure.
probable_cause: The right horizontal stabilizer rear spar fractured due to fatigue cracking caused by stiffer redesigned spar attachment fittings that prevented the structure from absorbing and transferring stresses from gust loads. The crack developed in a concealed location not accessible during routine maintenance, so it went undetected. The fail-safe design proved invalid when complete rear spar failure resulted in total loss of pitch control.

summary: Japan Air Lines Flight 715, a McDonnell Douglas DC-8-62H, was on approach to Subang Airport in Malaysia on September 27, 1977. The crew continued descending in instrument meteorological conditions until the aircraft struck a hill near the Elmina Estate, 4 miles from the airport. title: 1977 Benghazi Libyan Arab Airlines Tu-154 crash
summary: A Tu-154A leased from Balkan Bulgarian Airlines carrying 159 hajj pilgrims and 6 crew took off from Jiddah for Benghazi. Egyptian airspace was closed to Libyan aircraft, requiring an indirect route that was longer than planned. The crew did not plan for the longer flight time, leaving the aircraft short of fuel. Heavy fog blanketed Benghazi airport, preventing landing. After failing to locate the alternate airport, the aircraft ran out of fuel and made a forced landing, killing 59 occupants.

title: Malaysian Airline System 653
summary: Malaysian Airline System Flight 653 was hijacked as it descended toward Kuala Lumpur on 4 December 1977. Someone knocked on the cockpit door and one or more hijackers suddenly barged into the cockpit. The pilots were forced to cut off all communications. Investigators heard a series of gunshots on the cockpit voice recorder and concluded that both pilots were fatally shot, leaving the aircraft professionally uncontrolled until it impacted the ground at near-vertical angle at Tanjung Kupang, killing all 100 people aboard.

title: United Airlines 2860

summary: United Airlines Flight 2860, a DC-8 cargo flight, departed San Francisco at 23:17 PST on December 17, 1977, with an intermediate stop at Salt Lake City. Near Salt Lake City at 01:11 MST, the crew reported electrical trouble and entered a holding pattern. While holding, the flight was absent from approach control frequency for 7.5 minutes and entered an area of hazardous terrain. When the controller warned of terrain on the right and told the crew to climb to 8,000 ft, they acknowledged but 11 seconds later crashed into a 7,665 ft mountain ridge at 7,200 ft.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determined the cause was the controller's issuance of an incomplete and ambiguous holding clearance and the flight crew's acceptance of it. The crew failed to adhere to established lack-of-communication guidelines and holding procedures. Aircraft electrical problems were a contributing factor.
